methodological_rigor.justification: Secondary analysis of a Phase 2 TNT trial (NCT04380337) with clearly defined pre-/post-treatment MRI cohort, rigorous segmentation workflow (two annotators -> radiologist reference -> independent fellow), nnU-Net framework with 5-fold cross-validation, and a principled semi-supervised extension using pseudo-labels. DSC comparisons use paired t-tests and Wilcoxon signed-rank with BCa bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples), with appropriate discussion of discordant normality results. Key limitations include small reference-standard cohort (n=37), same 37 test cases used to evaluate Model 1 and Model 2 (the pseudo-label source model is evaluated on the same set whose radiologist segmentations informed the pseudo-label generation, though Model 1 was only trained on the 37 reference cases then applied to 81 additional unlabeled cases), single-center data, and the acknowledged spatial mismatch between T2W segmentations and ADC/sDWI features.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort / secondary analysis of a single-institution trial maps to LoE 2b. The clinical aim (supporting MRI-based cCR assessment for non-operative management) is genuinely important, but the current results are proof-of-concept: post-treatment segmentation performance is poor (DSC 0.175) and radiomic clustering, while showing cCR alignment, is unsupervised and not prospectively validated.

reporting_quality.justification: TRIPOD is the appropriate standard for a prediction/segmentation model. The manuscript reports data flow, model development, pre-processing, cross-validation, performance metrics with CIs and both parametric and non-parametric tests, and model-versus-rater comparisons. Importantly, the authors explicitly provide a code availability section (GitHub repository URL redacted in normalized text) with model weights and hyperparameters, which is above-average for the field. Some omissions: no calibration analysis on the radiomic clusters, no formal decision-curve or sensitivity/specificity at clinically meaningful thresholds, and a TRIPOD checklist is not included.

novelty_literature.justification: nnU-Net-based rectal tumor segmentation on MRI and ADC-based radiomics are active research areas; the specific contribution here is the controlled semi-supervised extension using pseudo-labels (n=37 -> n=118) and the unsupervised radiomic clustering that aligns with cCR status in TNT. This is a meaningful methodological demonstration rather than a paradigm shift, partly because the central clinical problem (post-treatment segmentation) remains unsolved (DSC 0.175).

writing_presentation.justification: Well-written, clearly structured manuscript with careful Methods, appropriately hedged Results interpretation, and a comprehensive Limitations section that acknowledges the T2W-ADC spatial mismatch, single-center nature, and reliance on a single radiologist's segmentations. Figures and tables are well described and numerical reporting is consistent. Minor issues: Equation 1 and Equation 2 are referenced but not rendered in the markdown; the outlier explanation in Figure 5 (SFX 002, 011, 029) is clear but could benefit from inclusion in the main Results text.

key_strengths: Rigorous nnU-Net workflow with 5-fold CV, semi-supervised extension, and bootstrap-based statistical inference on DSC differences
Data and code availability: model weights, hyperparameters, and training code stated as publicly available on GitHub
Thorough, self-critical Limitations section addressing T2W-ADC spatial mismatch, single-radiologist reference, and single-center scope
Unsupervised radiomic clustering aligns with cCR status without using labels, suggesting genuine biological signal even in a small cohort
Clear quantitative improvement from semi-supervised training (Model 1 DSC 0.682 -> Model 2 DSC 0.769 vs radiologist)
key_concerns: Post-treatment segmentation (Model 3) DSC of 0.175 is very poor and limits near-term clinical utility, as the authors acknowledge
Small reference cohort (n=37) and single-institution data; radiomic clustering finding needs external validation
Radiomic analysis performed on ADC maps using T2W-derived segmentations without registration; authors flag this but it remains a methodological weakness
No calibration or decision-curve analysis; performance metrics at clinically meaningful sensitivity/specificity thresholds are not reported
Equations 1 and 2 referenced in Methods but not rendered in the manuscript
chief_reviewer.rationale: A technically sound proof-of-concept that honestly reports both its successes (semi-supervised improvement) and its core unresolved challenge (post-treatment segmentation); fits a mid-tier imaging/oncology journal after minor revisions resolving missing equations and adding explicit performance thresholds.
